speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I wish to address Assoc Prof Razwana’s question about online solemnisations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Following the 2022 amendments to the AMLA, ROMM has been empowered to conduct solemnisations via remote communication technology, in addition to physical solemnisations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: ROMM had consulted the Office of the Mufti to put in steps to ensure that online solemnisations will meet all the requirements of a valid Muslim marriage under Muslim law.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, again, it is subject to the approval of the Office of the Mufti.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This option for online solemnisations will provide for unique situations like the COVID-19 pandemic when people were not able to meet physically.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Notwithstanding this, physical solemnisations will continue to be the default norm and preferred mode.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our Kadi and Naib Kadi will ensure this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The SYC has published detailed videos and user guides, as well as set up a call centre helpdesk, to help users navigate the digital portal.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC will continue to take in feedback to enhance the user experience.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim raised a number of questions and suggestions regarding the SYC-related amendments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is because SYC’s jurisdiction is matrimonial in nature, limited to hearing child maintenance matters upon a dissolution of a Muslim marriage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is common that parties already have ongoing maintenance proceedings in FJC even before the divorce proceedings are commenced in SYC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Enforcement of maintenance orders are also carried out in the FJC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is thus more convenient for parties, as a matter of practice, for a single Court, the FJC, to hear all matters relating to maintenance of children, including the enforcement of these orders.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This also prevents the possibility that two contrary maintenance orders are made by two separate Courts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To Assoc Prof Razwana's query, I would like to assure the Member that the FJC can make orders on maintenance for a child above 21 years old if they are mentally or physically disabled.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, on how the Court will exercise its expanded powers under the new sections 36B and 43(2).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As no two cases are alike, the Court will make its determination based on the specific facts of each case on whether the legal threshold has been met.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Presidents and Registrars of the Court will do so with a view to ensuring that the rules of natural justice will also be preserved and given effect to, including dealing with the case expeditiously to protect the welfare of the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, Mr Zhulkarnain had suggested that we expand the Syariah Court’s jurisdiction and powers beyond what this Bill is introducing today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Specifically, Mr Zhulkarnain suggested that the Syariah Court be empowered to make decisions on the division of matrimonial assets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He cited the 2017 case of TMO vs TMP, where the Court of Appeal allowed the appeal by the wife to seek an order from the FJC for division of her matrimonial assets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This was after the Court of Appeal confirmed that the High Court retained residual jurisdiction over matters like the division of matrimonial assets, which do not fall within the jurisdiction of the Syariah Court.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, there is no legal vacuum and parties to a foreign Muslim divorce can proceed to the civil courts to claim financial relief and are not left stranded without recourse.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will study carefully Mr Zhulkarnain's other suggestions for the Syariah Court, along with other feedback we received from stakeholders such as the Muslim Law Practice Committee of the Law Society of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This study will be done in consultation with the legal and asatizah fraternities, together with the broader Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Assoc Prof Razwana asked about the proposed enhancements to the Syariah Court’s judge-led approach for divorce cases and how the Court can connect individuals with relevant community services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I wish to clarify that the judge-led approach is actually already an existing practice of the Syariah Court.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These amendments enhance the Court’s ability to apply the judge-led approach.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Currently, the Court is also empowered to make child- and family-centric social support referrals where it deems appropriate, both in the course of proceedings and after the divorce is finalised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One example is to refer parties to counselling.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am heartened by the ideas and suggestions from our community leaders and other stakeholders during the public consultations and in this debate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have incorporated some of these ideas in this amendment Bill and will explore others as we implement the changes with our statutory Muslim institutions and community partners.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do any Member have any clarifications to seek from Minister?
